name: Northern Arc Capital Ltd
tagline: Recently-listed diversified NBFC (~Rs 4,850 Cr) trading ~1.2x book / ~11x earnings, growing AUM ~26% and PAT ~41%, with asset quality now improving QoQ, credit cost falling (3.2% -> 2.6%) and D2C own-book mix at ~64% - the ROE inflection to mid-teens is the re-rating lever, capped by an ~11-12% blended ROE today and a big FY25 AUM guidance miss on the record
business_overview: Northern Arc operates two segments: (1) direct-to-consumer (D2C) lending across MSME, MFI, LAP, 2-wheeler, consumer and housing - now ~64% of AUM (Rs ~10,800 Cr, +51% YoY) and higher NIM; (2) 'credit solutions' - originating and placing loans for other financial institutions via its Nimbus platform (declining share). Also runs investment management (NAIM - launched a Rs 1,000-1,500 Cr Finserve AIF and a USD 65m climate fund in 2026), an advisory arm and 'AltiFi' (retail bond platform). RBI granted factoring-business approval in 2026. ~450 branches, adding 50-60 this year. Professionally/institutionally owned - no promoter.
fundamentals_table: Lending AUM Rs 16,855 Cr Jun-2026 (+26% YoY); FY26 PAT Rs 406 Cr (+33% YoY); Q1 FY27 PAT Rs 114 Cr (+41% YoY)
GNPA 1.0% / NNPA 0.5% (Jun 2026, both improved ~20/15 bps QoQ); Rs 66 Cr overlap/management provision retained from Mar-2026
NIM 9.3-9.4% (guidance ~10%); credit cost 2.6% Q1 FY27, down from 3.2% Q4 FY25; FY27 guide 2.3-2.8%
~1.24x book / ~11x earnings; listed Sep 2024; brokerage 12-m target ~Rs 350
fundamentals_narrative: A cheap, fast-growing NBFC with a differentiated model: through the last 5 years of MFI/consumer stress that produced large write-offs at many peers, Northern Arc kept credit costs contained, and they are now normalising down (Q4 FY25 3.2% -> FY26 2.8% -> Q1 FY27 2.6%). The deep-dive established that asset quality is genuinely improving, not just optically: GNPA/NNPA both fell ~20/15 bps QoQ in Q1 FY27 to 1.0%/0.5%, and the long-standing 'low NPA / high credit cost' criticism has a credible structural answer - unsecured loans are written off at 90 DPD, so they never sit in the NPA bucket while the credit-cost line absorbs them. The mix shift to higher-NIM own-book D2C lending has accelerated (50% -> 59% FY26 -> 64% Q1 FY27; target >two-thirds). Growth is solid (AUM +26%, PAT +41%) and the stock trades at ~1.24x book. The reservations: blended ROE is still only ~11-12% (below cost of equity; the 16-18% three-year target is untested), management missed its FY25 AUM guidance badly (25-27% guided vs 16.4% delivered) before recalibrating and hitting FY26 numbers precisely, Q3 FY26 flagged emerging stress in unsecured business loans and small-ticket LAP, and no promoter is cited as a reason the market is slow to re-rate.
technical_read: Not independently pulled. Up ~25% over 12 months and ~20% over 6 months; trades ~1.24x book, mid of a Rs 206-334 52-week range.
sentiment_summary: Read the most recent ~16 of 51 posts (Feb 2026 to Aug 2026). hitesh2710 (elevated, invested) is the clearest positive: 'consistency continues in Q1 FY27... slightly differentiated business model vs run-of-the-mill NBFCs... even during the past 5 years when others suffered massive write-offs, Northern Arc remained a model of consistency. If and when markets recognise this company for what I feel it is, one can see good returns.' thakurvi (invested) notes the mix shift to own-book/higher-NIM lending, which should attract a better multiple. aditya14920251 shared a detailed 3-part blog ('Smart money is quietly buying this Rs 4,000 Cr NBFC'). Counter-weight: murali603 (elevated) is on the sidelines - 'I will enter once they start reducing provisions... NPA numbers always on the lower side and credit cost on the higher side since listing.' Snowman/thakurvi discussed the one-time digital-book ECL as the cause of the Q3 price fall.
community_signal: One genuine positive conviction signal from an elevated, invested member (hitesh2710) on the quality/consistency of the model. Balanced by an elevated member (murali603) who is deliberately waiting on the sidelines over asset-quality optics - a concern the FY26/Q1 FY27 filings substantially answer (credit cost falling, GNPA/NNPA improving QoQ, 90-DPD write-off explanation). Net: a credible quality endorsement, not a unanimous one.
bse_notes: IPO September 2024. Q2 to Q3 FY26 credit cost rose ~Rs 92 Cr to ~Rs 130 Cr on a one-time ECL reassessment of the digital-lending book; an Rs 66 Cr overlap provision from that exercise is still retained as of Mar/Jun 2026. 2026 corporate actions: RBI approval to undertake factoring business; USD 65m maiden climate fund via Northern Arc Investments IFSC Trust; Rs 1,000 Cr (+Rs 500 Cr green-shoe) Finserve AIF launched by NAIM; routine debt private placements. No equity dilution/QIP, no rating downgrade, no auditor or board-level red flag surfaced. No promoter (institutionally owned). No SEBI action; no red-flag tier.
bull_case: Cheap (~1.24x book, ~11x earnings) for AUM +26% / PAT +41% growth and an improving mix
Asset quality improving on the numbers - GNPA/NNPA both down QoQ in Q1 FY27; credit cost normalising 3.2% (Q4 FY25) -> 2.6% (Q1 FY27)
The 'low NPA / high credit cost' bear point has a credible structural answer (unsecured written off at 90 DPD, never enters the NPA bucket)
Mix shift to higher-NIM own-book D2C lending accelerating (50% -> 64% of AUM in a year) - the re-rating driver
ROE inflecting (Q4 FY26 14% vs 11.1% FY26 full-year); 3-year guide ROA 3.5-4% / ROE 16-18%, plus a trusted-user (hitesh2710) quality endorsement
Fee-income optionality: Nimbus co-lending platform, AltiFi retail bonds, new factoring licence, Rs 1,000 Cr+ AIF
bear_case: Blended ROE still only ~11-12% - below cost of equity, and the 16-18% three-year target is untested
Management missed FY25 AUM guidance badly (25-27% guided vs 16.4% delivered) before recalibrating - guidance credibility is 'mixed', not proven
Q3 FY26 flagged emerging stress in unsecured business loans and small-ticket LAP - the next MFI-style pattern to watch
Fee income has run below its own 110-120 bps target (~70-90 bps) - platform monetisation is slow
MFI-cycle and consumer-credit exposure; sector sentiment weak; no promoter has historically meant a slower re-rating
A true 10x from ~Rs 4,850 Cr in 2-3 years is unrealistic for an NBFC - brokerages see ~1.3-1.6x over that horizon; the honest base case is a 2-3x on re-rating plus compounding
verdict_headline: 10x-in-2-3-years label retained at MEDIUM-HIGH conviction - a cheap NBFC (~1.2x book) improving on every axis this pass (asset quality, credit cost, D2C mix, Q4 ROE 14%), with the main asset-quality-optics bear point substantially answered; realistically a 2-3x re-rating-plus-compounding, held short of higher conviction by an ~11-12% blended ROE and a big FY25 guidance miss on record
verdict_reasoning: Kept as '10x-in-2-3-years' under the four-box gate (score 3.0: tam yes, valuation yes) - a small/mid-cap at 1.24x book with 26% AUM growth, accelerating mix shift and a genuine ROE inflection path; the return-magnitude label is permitted with the standing caveat that the realistic base case is a 2-3x, not a literal 10x

Conviction raised MEDIUM -> MEDIUM-HIGH: the FY26 AR and Q1 FY27 concall confirm the thesis - credit cost down 3.2% -> 2.6%, GNPA/NNPA improving QoQ, D2C mix 50% -> 64%, Q4 FY26 ROE 14% - and give a credible structural answer to murali603's 'low NPA / high credit cost' concern (unsecured written off at 90 DPD)
Held short of High by the ~11-12% blended ROE (below CoE), the untested 16-18% target, the FY25 AUM guidance miss, slow fee-income monetisation and Q3 FY26's emerging unsecured-book stress
No red-flag tier. Re-check on: 2-3 quarters of credit cost <=2.5%, ROA crossing 3.0%, ROE holding mid-teens, and whether the unsecured/LAP stress spreads

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: At ~1.24x book / ~11x earnings the market implies mid-teens book-value CAGR with ROE stuck around 11-12%. A re-rating toward ~1.8-2x book requires ROE sustained at 15%+, i.e. roughly 20-25% EPS CAGR FY26-28 against a ~16-18x fair exit multiple.
market_expectation.our_fy27_estimate: PAT +30-35% (~Rs 520-550 Cr) on 24-26% AUM growth, NIM ~9.5%, credit cost ~2.5%, ROA ~3.0%
market_expectation.our_fy28_estimate: PAT +25-30%, ROA 3.3-3.5%, ROE 14-15% as opex leverage and fee income build
market_expectation.gap_basis: The price embeds ROE staying ~11-12%; the D2C mix shift, credit-cost normalisation and opex leverage point to 15%+ ROE by FY28, which supports a re-rating toward 1.8-2x book. The stock's 25% 12-month run shows the market sees the growth but not yet the full return-on-equity re-rating.
market_expectation.data_caveat: no broker consensus; implied path is a reverse-P/E estimate + screener.in forward figures + VP thread view

catalyst.event: 2-3 consecutive quarters of credit cost <=2.5% plus ROA crossing 3.0%, confirming the ROE inflection toward mid-teens

value_chain.position: multi-sector originate-and-hold lender plus a debt-market platform (Nimbus) that originates and places loans for other financial institutions
value_chain.bottleneck_node: cost of funds + through-cycle underwriting discipline
value_chain.note: MFI/unsecured supply is consolidating after the FY24-25 stress - survivors with intact underwriting (Northern Arc kept credit costs contained) gain share and pricing. Funding cost and cycle management gate the returns.

drivers: D2C own-book mix shift raising blended yield (structural)
credit-cost normalisation off the FY25 MFI peak (cyclical)
operating leverage on the branch build (structural)
earnings_quality.normalised_note: ROA ~2.8% is mid-cycle and below management's 3.5-4% aspiration; credit cost 2.6% is still above a ~2% normalised level. Earnings are in recovery, not at a peak - the risk is the recovery stalling, not mean-reversion from a high.

growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: AUM YoY roughly steady 22-26% across the last 4-6 quarters. PAT YoY oldest->newest: ~+24% (Q3 FY26), +251% (Q4 FY26, depressed prior-year base), +41% (Q1 FY27) - underlying PAT growth accelerating on credit-cost relief and mix.
growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: ~11x trailing earnings needs only ~15% EPS CAGR to hold; realised/near-term PAT growth (30%+) clears that comfortably, leaving the upside in a P/B re-rating if ROE reaches mid-teens.

management_quality.capital_allocation: Reinvests all earnings into AUM at an ~11-14% ROE (below cost of equity today, targeted to mid-teens); no dividend yet (policy 'under board debate'); no unrelated diversification - factoring, climate fund and the Finserve AIF are all on-strategy adjacencies.
management_quality.capability_ladder_note: Explicit move up the value curve: originate-and-distribute -> higher-yield own-book D2C retail; building fee-income platforms (Nimbus co-lending, AltiFi retail bonds, factoring).

four_box.note: tailwind weak (retail-credit formalisation is real but MFI/unsecured cycle exposure and weak sector sentiment offset it); moat weak (multi-sector underwriting data + through-cycle discipline, but NBFC lending is not a structural moat). tam yes (Rs 16,855 Cr book in a huge market) and valuation yes (1.24x book / 11x earnings not pricing the ROE re-rating) carry it to 3.0 -> return-magnitude label permitted; realistic base case is a 2-3x.
